pages.text: Mrs. Goose's goslings had played in the yard, peep, peep. But now not one was in sight.
Mrs. Goose stamped her feet. "My babies!" "I will find them and bring them back," Pipo said, setting off.
Her shout filled the yard. "Babies! Where are you? Come out at once!"
Grass rustled and shook. Only a grasshopper leaped away from her voice.
Behind the shed, she shouted louder. "Come out, or Mom will be angry!"
The yard was utterly silent. Her neck drooped. "Why does nobody answer?!"
She sank to the ground. "Oh, my babies..."
Pipo raised a hand. "Shh." When the yard grew quiet, a tiny peep, peep came from somewhere.
He gently parted a bush. The goslings slept huddled together, peeping in their dreams.
Pipo brought them back in a little line. Mrs. Goose wrapped her wings around them. "I must tell the whole village this story!"
